scenes.act: AI Has Accelerated Coding, Not Software Delivery
scenes.title: Faster coding is only the beginning.
scenes.takeaway: The bottleneck moves from producing code to agreeing intent, carrying it through and judging the result.
scenes.presenterNotes: Say: Nattu has established the lifecycle problem. Land: faster generation is useful, but it is not the same as dependable delivery.

scenes.act: AI Has Accelerated Coding, Not Software Delivery
scenes.title: The request is simple. The behaviour isn’t.
scenes.takeaway: The first useful output is not code. It is a decision-ready set of questions.
scenes.presenterNotes: Show: select Capture & Refine, then open its role and skill files. Do: point to the separate domain context.

scenes.act: Reimagining the Lifecycle, From Code Generation to Confidence
scenes.title: Turn the request into an agreement.
scenes.takeaway: Capture & Refine creates a shared, testable agreement — not merely a longer document.
scenes.presenterNotes: Prepared walkthrough. Do not describe this as a live autonomous run.

scenes.act: Reimagining the Lifecycle, From Code Generation to Confidence
scenes.title: Separate what travels from what belongs here.
scenes.takeaway: The questions can travel across products. The business answers usually cannot.
scenes.presenterNotes: Show: expand the full skill, then the domain file. Land: domain truth remains human-owned.

scenes.act: Reimagining the Lifecycle, From Code Generation to Confidence
scenes.title: Carry intent through six explicit decisions.
scenes.takeaway: Intent → Build → Prove → Merge → Release → Learn.
scenes.presenterNotes: Keep merge and release as separate decisions. Then move to Nattu’s four capabilities.

scenes.act: The Four Capabilities of an Agentic SDLC
scenes.title: Four capabilities make the lifecycle dependable.
scenes.kicker: THE FOUR CAPABILITIES OF AN AGENTIC SDLC
scenes.takeaway: Capability connects faster production to confidence and control.
scenes.presenterNotes: Use these exact capability names. Do not rename them as the four journey chapters.

scenes.act: From Theory to Practice, One Change Travels Through the SDLC
scenes.title: Design makes the behaviour visible before planning the build.
scenes.takeaway: Design precedes planning so implementation is not forced to invent the user experience.
scenes.presenterNotes: Land the sequence explicitly: Capture & Refine → Design → Planner.

scenes.act: From Theory to Practice, One Change Travels Through the SDLC
scenes.title: The plan names the path and the proof.
scenes.takeaway: A plan is useful when the Builder and Tester can tell what done means.
scenes.presenterNotes: Show: role and skill source. Point out the explicit stop condition.

scenes.act: From Theory to Practice, One Change Travels Through the SDLC
scenes.title: Build the bounded change — and preserve the agreement.
scenes.takeaway: The Builder does not silently resolve product ambiguity in code.
scenes.presenterNotes: Use the worked-example file if present; label all example artefacts as prepared.

scenes.act: From Theory to Practice, One Change Travels Through the SDLC
scenes.title: Evidence answers a claim — not every possible question.
scenes.takeaway: Not run is not passed. Old evidence does not prove the current change.
scenes.presenterNotes: Do not invent execution results. Open repository evidence only when present.

scenes.act: Closing the Confidence Gaps, What Changed?
scenes.title: Why should we trust this change?
scenes.takeaway: Leadership needs the basis for confidence — not a fabricated product score.
scenes.presenterNotes: Land: merge confidence is not release confidence. Do not imply an NFR X-ray or merge score was executed.

scenes.act: Closing the Confidence Gaps, What Changed?
scenes.title: Ready to merge is not ready to release.
scenes.takeaway: A reviewed change is not a blanket guarantee about the production system.
scenes.presenterNotes: No product score is shown; no release claim is made.

scenes.act: Closing the Confidence Gaps, What Changed?
scenes.title: One finding can improve three different things.
scenes.takeaway: The loop closes only when learning changes a later decision or delivery outcome.
scenes.presenterNotes: Show: Curator source files. Land: version, review, maintain and recheck.

scenes.title: Scale the method — not uncontrolled access.
scenes.takeaway: Permission to inspect a repository does not imply permission to deploy.
scenes.presenterNotes: No claim of enterprise adoption. This is an operating pattern for evaluation.

scenes.title: Adopt around one bottleneck, then inspect the result.
scenes.takeaway: The objective is a better accepted outcome — not the cheapest first answer.
scenes.presenterNotes: The free 90-minute masterclass refers to the overall event. This contribution’s working 50-minute slot remains provisional. Do not imply a human rehearsal occurred.

scenes.title: Start with one bottleneck. Improve the next change.
scenes.takeaway: Every feature can improve the product, the domain understanding and the capability used next time.
scenes.presenterNotes: Reset returns to the opening. Recovery: PDF and PPTX carry the same scene sequence offline.
